question.text: The standard electrode potential (<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup><mo>/</mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>) for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>Cr</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mi>Mn</mi></math> & <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Co</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>26</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>-</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>41</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>57</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>97</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>, respectively. The metal ions which can liberate <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> from a dilute acid are

solution.text:
The E⊝ values for the redox couple (M3+/M2+) shows that Mn2+ and Co2+ ions are the strongest oxidising agents in aqueous solution.

The ions Ti2+, V2+ and Cr2+ are strong reducing agents and will liberate hydrogen from a dilute acid.

So, the Correct answer is V2+ and Cr2+.
